result:
I've made the sign-up changes for all five reports, following ADR 0003 (the product note loses where they disagree). The full suite (617 tests) and typecheck pass, and eslint is clean on the changed files. I also ran sign-ups through a scratch script against a temporary database. I didn't add or change any tests.

**1. Names that broke sign-up.** `register` passed a raw slug to `createOrganization`, which refuses reserved or too-short slugs after the user row is already written. The slug is now derived first, so none of these names refuses a sign-up:
- A name that slugifies to a reserved word gets a suffix: "Admin" becomes `admin-2`, then `admin-3` for the next one.
- "J", "山田" and other names with nothing usable fall back to `workspace`, then `workspace-2` and so on.
- I fixed `uniqueSlug` as well. Shortening a long slug could leave a trailing hyphen and produce an invalid `abc--2`.

**2. Email case.** Addresses are now lowercased when stored and compared lowercased on lookup, so `Alice@Example.com` and `alice@example.com` are one account at sign-up and sign-in. Lookup also finds old mixed-case rows, and if legacy data holds two spellings of one address it picks the oldest. I did not merge or fix any existing duplicate accounts; that needs a separate decision.

**3. Throttling.**
- **Sign-up bucket:** sign-up is charged once per attempt on `auth:register` before anything is read or written. I set the bucket to 10 attempts, refilling 2 per minute; that figure is my choice, since the ADR doesn't give one.
- **Error mapping:** `toAppError` now maps `RateLimitedError` to `rate_limited` (HTTP 429) with a "wait a moment and try again" message. The service's sign-in and reset-confirm throttles now throw `RateLimitedError` instead of a plain `Error`, so people are told to wait.
- **Reset request:** a throttled password-reset request now returns a silent success from its action. Without that, the new mapping would have made it visibly say "too many attempts", which the ADR rules out.

**4. Existing address.** It now throws a new `EmailTakenError` (code `conflict`) before anything is written, and the error mapper turns it into a `conflict` result. A concurrent sign-up that loses on the unique index gets the same error.

**5. Workspace name.** The name is `<display name>'s workspace`, with the display name shortened (without splitting an emoji) until the whole name fits the 64-character limit and still ends in `'s workspace`. I added `ORG_NAME_MAX_LENGTH` to `src/schemas/organization.ts` and used it in the create and update schemas.

The main changes are in `src/server/services/auth-service.ts`, `src/server/repositories/user-repository.ts`, `src/lib/errors.ts`, `src/lib/slug.ts` and a new `src/lib/email.ts`.
